A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same convergence-analysis work. All 22 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2, including equations and appendices, are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 presents theoretical convergence results and proofs. Neither the main text nor its appendices reports original experiments, simulations, or data analyses.

after.justification: V2 remains a theoretical paper. Its expanded appendices contain mathematical arguments rather than original empirical results.

M1.justification: The SAG, SAGA, and IAG updates and sampling schemes are retained. The variant that collects gradients without updating iterates during burn-in was already described after v1 Lemma 3.10; v2 adds its derivation, not a new procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical training/evaluation tasks. Strongly convex, non-convex, and Markov-sampling settings are treated theoretically in both.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. Discussions of GD, SGD, and other variance-reduction algorithms concern theoretical guarantees and prior work.

E3.justification: No experimental protocols are present in either version. The stepsize and staleness choices in the corresponding main convergence theorems remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, error analyses, or case studies. The added burn-in argument is a theoretical proof.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. The retained high-probability convergence bounds are theoretical guarantees.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added or revised. The principal strongly convex, non-convex, Markov-sampling, and IAG convergence-rate formulas remain identical after renumbering; supplementary mathematical changes are covered under T1.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix B.2 adds a derivation claiming V_tau <= 2L||x*||_2^2 for the previously described modified burn-in scheme. V2 also explicitly discusses nonzero initialization and removes v1 Section 3.4's PL-condition linear-convergence extension. The main theorems remain unchanged. The original burn-in calculation changes 36/256 in v1 Eq. (51) to 35/256 in v2 Eq. (43), an apparent arithmetic typo that leaves the final stated bound unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a unified proof for SAG/SAGA/IAG, high-probability SAG/SAGA guarantees, non-convex and Markov-sampling extensions, and improved theoretical IAG rates. Abstract and conclusion edits do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation of failure-probability dependence in the convergence exponent, explicitly acknowledges required prior knowledge of the horizon in Remark 3.13, and distinguishes prospective single-loop extensions from double-loop methods in Section 5. It removes v1's explicit caveat that the delayed-GD lower bound might not apply to this setting.

D1.justification: Initialization, zero-filled gradient memory, stepsize rules, and the optional burn-in procedure are already documented in v1. V2 adds theoretical explanations but no implementation, hardware, runtime, or code/data-access information.

R1.justification: V2 adds Koloskova et al. (2023) for non-convex incremental-gradient work and Lattimore and Szepesvari (2020) for the doubling trick. It removes Karimi et al. (2016), Shalev-Shwartz and Ben-David (2014), and Wright and Recht (2022). The principal positioning around unified variance-reduction analysis is retained.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the SGD/SAGA background and several proof explanations, moves smoothness/convexity facts into Appendix A, reorganizes the proof appendices, and expands the conclusion. It also adds acknowledgments and an impact statement. The main section sequence and most of the argument remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the single-column main text and references with a two-column conference layout, changes typography and headers, and removes the colored theorem/lemma boxes. Appendices retain single-column presentation. Neither version contains figures or tables.

improvement.justification: V2 improves discussion of horizon requirements and applicability, but the new Appendix B.2 does not clearly justify Eq. (44): partially populated gradient memories can produce nonzero estimators even when x0 = x* = 0, where its bound vanishes. V2 also removes v1's lower-bound applicability caveat. With the central theorems unchanged, useful clarification and unresolved mathematical justification coexist, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
